pr_title: fix(Notion (Beta) Node): Fix create database page fails if relation param is empty/undefined

issue_context.title: Notion: Create page node fails when relation is empty
comments:
Here is an example of how you could modify your workflow to solve the issue without changing the implementation of the Notion node:

- Remove the `Relation IDs` field from the `Create Page` node.
- Connect the `Create Page` node to a `Conditional` node.
- In the `Conditional` node, set up a condition to check if the value for the relation property exists in the payload. For example, you could use an expression like `{{$node["Create Page"].json['categoryId']}}` to check if the Category relation property is set in the payload.
- If the condition is true, connect the `True` output of the `Conditional` node to a `Update Page` node.
- In the `Update Page` node, set the `Page ID` to the ID of the page that was created by the `Create Page` node. You can use the ID field from the Create Page node output as the value for the Page ID field.
- In the `Update Page` node, set the relational property to the value you want to update. For example, you could use an expression like `{{$node["Before Create Page"].json["categoryId"]}}` to set the Category relation property to the value that was passed to the `Create Page` node.
- Connect the `False` output of the `Conditional` node to the next node in your workflow. This will allow the workflow to continue if the relation property is not set in the payload.

This solution will allow you to create a page without setting the relation property, and then update the page with the relation property if it is available. It will avoid the error that occurs when the Relation IDs expression returns null, undefined, or an empty array, and allow you to create the page even if the relation property is not set.

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any further questions.

Hi @papykhader,
Thanks for reporting this issue and hinting at the fix. And apologies for the delay in getting back to you. We're tracking this bug internally as NODE-172 and will address it asap.
